output.brief:
What is going on: the departures are concentrated on one team, not spread across the group. Eight of the 11 associates assigned to Kestrel have resigned; only 1 of the 13 who weren't has. Pay doesn't explain it: salaries sit around the 54th–61st percentile, Brennick & Stowe's premium is £3–5k rather than £15k, and six of the eight leavers with known new pay took equal or lower pay. The hours target and job market affect everyone, and the first resignation came before the target rose.

What I can't tell you: Kestrel and Dorian Faulk arrived together. Every Kestrel associate reports to him and he supervises nothing else, so the records can't show whether workload, his supervision, or both is responsible.

How sure: very confident it's specific to the Kestrel team, not pay, targets or the market; undecided between workload and supervision.

What to do: don't announce the £12k payment or close the review. Commission the £9k independent interviews now (three weeks; four leavers have agreed), designed to separate supervision from workload, then choose between changing supervision or funding contract reviewers. Meanwhile, add matter and supervising partner to attrition reporting.
